synopsis: The cross-sector search found marketed products but no published validation method, duration or physical-testing share demonstrating substantially reduced physical validation; this is a research gap, not proof that relevant cases are absent [f15773, f1413, f2019]. Bosch’s tram system combines camera and radar with warnings and automatic braking, with public-transport approval reported by 2016, but its development duration, validation split and approval evidence package remain undisclosed in the research; other rail systems were not investigated deeply [f1417, f1420, f1421, f1422, f1423, f1424]. Wabtec’s December 2021 Komatsu haul-truck tests demonstrated controlled deceleration up to 30 km/h, followed by further physical testing to adjust detection zones for speed, payload, braking distance and road grade [f15781, f15782]. The neighboring-sector analogues require care: Kalmar’s June 2024 port case demonstrates warnings rather than stated automatic braking, Toyota SEnS+ slows through power cut-off rather than braking to a stop, and no currently sold agricultural or forestry system with documented object-triggered emergency braking and a public operating envelope was found [f1415, f15785, f15786, f1693]. The glossary concludes that the search supports no roughly four-month precedent from first representative hardware to accepted validation, but its categorical wording is stronger than the research’s explicit distinction between cases not found and cases confirmed absent [f15792, f2019].
